co_castlewood_canyon_sp.blurb: Castlewood Canyon is a shallow gorge on the plains southeast of Denver, cut by Cherry Creek through a hard layer of cobbles cemented together by volcanic ash. The cliffs are short, mostly under 25 meters, and steep, which makes this a place for quick laps rather than long days. Bouldering makes up around half of the climbing, with problems from V0 to the high V-grades and a particularly even spread through the lower and middle grades. The rest is a mix of sport, trad and top-rope, centered on 5.9 to 5.12 with some easier lines too. Many trad cracks are lightly climbed. Larger zones include the Five and Dime and Fountainbleau areas and the Grocery Store Walls. Winter can bring a little ice.

ca_angeles_national_forest.blurb: The Angeles National Forest covers most of the San Gabriel Mountains just north of greater Los Angeles, with terrain running from about 1,200 feet of chaparral country up to alpine-feeling peaks above 10,000 feet. Climbing is scattered across many pockets rather than one hub. Sport routes lead the way, followed by bouldering, with a smaller amount of trad, top-rope and a few ice and aid lines. Sport grades cluster from 5.8 to 5.12, and the boulders run from easy to hard with plenty of moderates. Granite is the rock at Williamson Rock, which is steep and technical. Other bigger zones are Texas Canyon, Horse Flats and the Mount Baldy Road crags. Expect a lot of driving between them.

ca_santa_monica_mountains.blurb: The Santa Monica Mountains run along the coast west of Los Angeles, a Mediterranean-climate range of about 250 square miles with deep canyons and odd rock formations. Sport climbing dominates, with a large bouldering scene next and a modest amount of top-rope and trad. Most sport routes fall between 5.9 and 5.12, with a solid group of 5.13s for strong climbers, and the boulders are mostly easy to mid-grade. Echo Cliffs is the best-known sport crag, with pockets and blocky holds on vertical to overhanging walls and a sunny feel; fall, winter and spring are the comfortable seasons there. Malibu Creek State Park is the other major draw, and smaller crags such as Saddle Peak and Point Dume fill in the map.

bc_stawamus_chief.blurb: The Stawamus Chief is a huge granodiorite dome beside the town of Squamish, rising steeply above Howe Sound and split by gullies into three summits. Glaciers carved its walls, and they now hold long, varied lines, from runout slabs to splitter cracks to bolted faces. It sits close to sea level, so the climbing here is rock rather than alpine or ice. Bouldering is the largest group of problems, much of it in the Grand Wall Boulders and North Wall Boulders, from easy through hard grades. Trad is the main roped style, mostly 5.9 to 5.12, with a small amount of sport. The Apron and the Bulletheads are other big sections, along with the North Walls and the Dihedrals.

nm_las_cruces_area_climbing.blurb: Climbing around Las Cruces centers on a few desert ranges beside the city. The Organ Mountains, a jagged ridge of spires just to the east, hold most of it: drive-up cragging, bouldering, and long adventurous peaks. The granitic Dona Ana Mountains to the north offer multi-pitch trad and boulders, and the Rough and Ready Hills have a short volcanic cliff band with a small set of sport routes. Trad and bouldering dominate the numbers. Roped routes are mostly 5.6 to 5.11, and the boulders run from V0 to V5 with fewer above that. Winters are very mild, which allows climbing year-round, though summer desert heat can be intense.

wa_frenchman_coulee_aka_vantage.blurb: Frenchman Coulee sits near Vantage in central Washington, where the cliffs show off tall columns of basalt. Cracks run between the columns, and the faces make for vertical, stemming-flavored sport climbing. It is best known as a winter crag, since the open faces catch sun at some point in the day. Sport leads, with trad close behind, and a small bouldering section. Grades concentrate from 5.8 to 5.11, with 5.10 the most common, and a few routes above 5.12. Echo Basin holds more than half of the climbs, including the Sunshine Wall. The Middle East Wall, the Feathers and North Rim are other major sections.
